# Reading research papers {#reading-ladder}

By the end of the QM learning line you will read the evidence in real
business and management research papers --- and in your own thesis sources
--- the way you now read a graph: systematically, and without being
intimidated. This page is your map. You never read a whole paper cold:
specific lectures assign one **bounded piece** of one paper (an abstract, a
descriptive table, one regression column), always with the same protocol.

## The six-question protocol

Whatever the paper, answer the same six questions about the piece you were
assigned:

1. **Claim:** What does the paper want readers to believe?
2. **Design:** What comparison is supposed to support that claim?
3. **Data:** What is the unit, sample, measurement, and missingness?
4. **Estimate:** Which number or figure carries the main result?
5. **Uncertainty:** How precise is the estimate, and what assumptions
   matter?
6. **Limitation:** What plausible alternative explanation remains?

Print these six questions or keep them open beside every paper you read ---
including for other courses and your thesis. They are the reading version of
the five-step graph sequence.

## Where you meet papers in this learning line

All papers are linked at their publishers; follow the DOI through the
university library for access. Read only the assigned piece --- full-paper
reading comes in Advanced.

| Where | Paper | What you read and do |
|---|---|---|
| [Lecture 1](../basic/b01-introduction-data-analysis.qmd) practice | [Ajzen (1991), the Theory of Planned Behavior](https://doi.org/10.1016/0749-5978(91)90020-T) | Title and abstract: separate theoretical constructs from measurable variables |
| [Lecture 5](../basic/b05-joint-covariance-correlation.qmd) practice | [Tierney & Farmer (2002), creative self-efficacy](https://doi.org/10.2307/3069429) | The descriptive-and-correlation table: read means, SDs, and one correlation with its limits |
| [Intermediate Lecture 3](../intermediate/i03-inference-fit-ftest.qmd) practice | Tierney & Farmer (2002), continued | One regression column: apply the estimate--SE--test--interval reading and find the reported $R^2$ |
| [Intermediate Lecture 4](../intermediate/i04-multiple-regression.qmd) practice | [Zhao, Seibert & Hills (2005), entrepreneurial intentions](https://doi.org/10.1037/0021-9010.90.6.1265) | Outcome, predictors, and controls: write the "holding fixed" sentence for one coefficient |
| [Intermediate Lecture 5](../intermediate/i05-categories-joint-tests.qmd) practice | [Brooks et al. (2014), entrepreneurial pitch success](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1321202111) | A categorical comparison: identify the category variable, the reference group, and what the gap does and does not show |
| Advanced (from spring) | [Van der Stede (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aos.2013.12.001); [Blood in the Water (2022), Shark Tank valuations](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbvi.2022.e00305); [Fitzsimmons & Douglas (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusvent.2010.01.001); [Koudstaal, Sloof & van Praag (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2015.2249); [Fazio, Guzman & Stern (2019)](https://www.nber.org/papers/w26099) | Designs, causal language, interactions, experiments, and panel evidence --- assigned within the Advanced course |

The 2022 Shark Tank valuation paper deserves a special mention: it analyses
a purpose-built research version of the same setting as our teaching data,
so in Advanced you will compare a published dataset against the file you
have worked with for three courses.

## How much to read

Each assigned piece is bounded on purpose: title and abstract, one methods
paragraph, one table or figure, one regression column, or one limitations
paragraph. If you find yourself reading page after page, you have left the
assignment. Depth comes from the six questions, not from volume.

::: {.callout-note}
## Where this ends up

By the end of Advanced, you should be able to annotate a paper as claim →
design → estimate → uncertainty → limitation, reproduce a central analysis
in R when materials permit, and explain why a statistical association is or
is not credible evidence for the paper's substantive claim --- the exact
skill your thesis will ask of you.
:::
